settings.shortcuts.handsFreeDesc: Best for talking at length: press once to start, press again to stop. Nothing to hold down.
settings.shortcuts.handsFreeHelp:
Which keys can I use?
A single common key (Right Alt, Caps Lock, F1–F24), a modifier + key combination, or a mouse side or middle button. Windows-reserved combinations that lock or switch windows or open system UI can't be bound.

What happens if I bind a mouse button?
Binding a side button takes over its Back and Forward function. Binding the middle button may break opening links in new tabs and autoscroll.
settings.shortcuts.pttDesc: Best for short bursts: recording starts once the whole combination is held down, and stops as soon as you release any key.
settings.shortcuts.pttHelp:
Which keys can I use?
A single common key (Caps Lock, F1–F24), a modifier + key combination, a modifier-only combination such as Ctrl + Win, or a mouse side or middle button. Windows-reserved combinations that lock or switch windows or open system UI can't be bound.

What are F13–F24?
Windows knows these keys, but keyboards rarely have them, so they almost never clash with other programs. A programmable keyboard or an external device with buttons can emit F13–F24 as a dedicated recording trigger; you can also remap a key you never use with a tool like PowerToys Keyboard Manager.

Do modifier-only combinations affect Windows?
Those keys still reach Windows, and some combinations may also open the Start menu. Try your choice in the apps you use most.

What happens if I bind a mouse button?
Binding a side button takes over its Back and Forward function. Binding the middle button may break opening links in new tabs and autoscroll.

On by default.
textFormat.normalizeNumbers.title: Normalize numbers
textFormat.normalizeNumbers.hint: Rewrites spelled-out Chinese numbers as digits, e.g. 三点一四 → 3.14, 百分之十五 → 15%
textFormat.normalizeNumbers.help:
Rewrites Chinese numbers that were spoken aloud into digits, which suits technical and data-heavy text better. Only converts when the intent is clear — it's best-effort.

三点一四 → 3.14
百分之十五 → 15%
GPT五点四 → GPT 5.4
扩容二十三台 → 扩容23台
两百五 → 250

To avoid false positives, a bare 一二三, set phrases such as 十全十美, and digit-by-digit numbers are left alone.
textFormat.stripTrailing.title: Drop end punctuation
textFormat.stripTrailing.hint: Removes punctuation at the end of each paragraph, keeping punctuation inside sentences
textFormat.stripTrailing.help:
Removes only the punctuation at the end of each paragraph. Punctuation inside a sentence, such as commas, stays. Handy when you paste transcripts straight into a chat box and don't want a trailing period.

With multiple paragraphs, every paragraph is handled, not just the last one.

你好，世界。→ 你好，世界
真的吗？！→ 真的吗
第一段。↵第二段！→ 第一段↵第二段
textFormat.punctuationToSpace.title: Punctuation to spaces
textFormat.punctuationToSpace.hint: Replaces all punctuation with spaces, e.g. 你好，世界！→ 你好 世界
textFormat.punctuationToSpace.help:
Replaces every punctuation mark with a space, collapses repeated spaces and trims the ends. Useful for keywords, search terms, or pasting somewhere that shouldn't carry punctuation. Decimal points and percent signs inside numbers are kept.

你好，世界！→ 你好 世界
第一，先做A；第二，再做B。→ 第一 先做A 第二 再做B
准确率是99.5%。→ 准确率是99.5%

dict.intro: Hotwords help speech recognition get proper nouns and industry terms right.
dict.caveat: Hotwords only raise the **chance of a match** — they don't guarantee it, and **more is not better**. Recognition services differ in how they handle hotwords; what your current setup does is explained below.
dict.delivery.sent: Hotwords are sent with every recognition.
dict.delivery.notSent: **The current recognition service does not send hotwords.**
dict.delivery.undecided: The API protocol for this service hasn't been detected yet, so whether hotwords apply is only known after the first recognition or a connection test.
dict.delivery.undecidedDeclaration: **SayIt hasn't recorded how this recognition service handles hotwords**, so it can't tell whether they will be sent this time. That's a gap on our side rather than a problem with your setup, and recognizing again won't change it — report it and we'll fill it in.
dict.delivery.undecidedQueryFailed: **SayIt couldn't read how the current service handles hotwords** — likely an older build or an internal call that failed. Recognizing again won't change this; try restarting SayIt, and if it persists, update to the latest version or report it.
dict.delivery.pathDependent: This model uses two different APIs depending on whether live captions are on, and hotwords behave differently on each; if the live connection fails, SayIt falls back to the other one.
dict.delivery.clientCap: You have **{count}** hotwords and SayIt sends at most **{cap}** per request; the rest are not sent. This is SayIt's own send limit, not a server restriction.
dict.delivery.fallbackHint: To still get these terms corrected: turn on "AI cleanup" and "Send hotwords to the AI prompt". Both switches are required, and it is skipped when a recording is too short or the AI call fails.
dict.delivery.spacingRestore: Hotwords are still used to restore spelling after recognition (for example turning "Say It" back into "SayIt"). That step needs no extra setup.
dict.delivery.openTable: See how each recognition service handles hotwords
dict.table.title: Hotword support by recognition service
dict.table.intro: This table is generated from what each service's implementation actually does — it is not a separately maintained list. **"Sent" only means hotwords go out with the recognition request; it does not guarantee a match.**
dict.table.capNote: SayIt sends at most {cap} per request
dict.table.unavailable: Hotword support information is unavailable right now. Restart SayIt and try again.
dict.table.otherModes: **Server mode**: sent — hotwords go to the server with every recognition. **Local models**: not sent — the local recognition engine has no hotword channel at present.
dict.table.footer: "OpenAI-compatible service" depends on the detected protocol: the chat-style API sends hotwords, the file transcription API does not. Run a connection test to see which one was detected. For services that don't send hotwords, hotwords are still used to restore spelling after recognition, and you can turn on "AI cleanup" plus "Send hotwords to the AI prompt" to have terms corrected during cleanup.
dict.countHint: You have **{count}** hotwords. **More is not better** — keep the list to terms you actually use.
dict.newCategoryPlaceholder: New category, e.g. Project A / Medical terms / Meeting terms
dict.orderHint: Category order sets hotword priority: when the total exceeds the limit the list is cut from the bottom, and some models only use the first part of it. Drag the handle at the top left of a card to move a category up.

err.server.timeout: The server took too long to respond. It may be starting up or under heavy load — try again shortly.
err.server.unreachable: Couldn't reach that address. Check the URL (including the https:// prefix), your network, and whether the service is running.
err.server.forbidden: The server refused the request (HTTP {status}). The address responds, but access is denied — make sure this is a SayIt backend and that a reverse proxy or firewall isn't blocking it.
err.server.notSayIt: That address responds, but there's no SayIt service on it. Enter the service root here, without a /api or /ws path.
err.server.internal: Server error (HTTP {status}). The address is right, the problem is on the server — check its logs.
err.provider.timeout: The provider took too long to respond. Try again shortly.
err.provider.unreachable: Couldn't reach the provider. Check your network, and whether you need a proxy to get there.
err.provider.badKey: The key was rejected. Check that it was copied in full with no stray spaces, and that the service is enabled in the provider's console.
err.provider.forbidden: The service refused the request (403) without pointing at the key. Usually that means it isn't offered in your region, or this account doesn't have the model enabled.
err.provider.rateLimit: The provider rate-limited this request. Please retry shortly, or check your call limits in their console.
err.provider.insufficientBalance: Your account balance is too low, so the request was not sent. Top up in the provider's console and retry.

asrProvider.doubaoBlurb: The most accurate for Chinese with live captions off, and fast.
asrProvider.qwenPlatformBlurb: Alibaba Bailian: one key covers all eight models. Choose Audio 3.1 for live captions, or Omni for recognition and cleanup in a single call.
asrProvider.qwenBlurb: Text arrives once you finish speaking. Even across languages, though not the top tier for Chinese.
asrProvider.qwenAudio31StreamBlurb: Pick this one for live captions: text appears as you speak, with the best accuracy and quick responses.
asrProvider.qwenAudioStreamBlurb: The previous generation, with the same capabilities as Audio 3.1. Keep it as a fallback if 3.1 gives you trouble.
asrProvider.qwenRealtimeBlurb: Also shows text as you speak, but Audio 3.1 does it better — and this one needs a workspace ID.
asrProvider.omniPlusBlurb: Recognition and cleanup in one step — no separate AI service needed.
asrProvider.omni38Blurb: The newest Omni generation, doing recognition and cleanup in one step, and you can point it at your own endpoint. No live captions.
asrProvider.omni38RealtimeBlurb: Same generation and same result as qwen3.8-omni-flash; this one goes through the official realtime endpoint and the address is fixed. Billing differs between the two, so check the pricing page before heavy use.
asrProvider.omniFlashBlurb: Like Omni Plus, faster and cheaper, slightly lower quality.
asrProvider.mimoBlurb: A fallback. Accuracy is middling; worth a try if you already have a Xiaomi API key. Does not send hotwords.
asrProvider.groqBlurb: Multilingual transcription with fast responses. Chinese is so-so, and it needs access to the international internet. Does not send hotwords.
asrProvider.openaiBlurb: Consistent across languages and accents, with good handling of technical terms and numbers. Requires an OpenAI account and access to the international internet.
asrProvider.openaiFileBlurb: One-shot transcription after recording. Top-tier accuracy, punctuation included. This API does not send hotwords.
asrProvider.openaiLiveBlurb: Text appears as you speak, and your hotwords are sent along as recognition context. Switches to file transcription when live captions are off, and that path does not send hotwords.
asrProvider.geminiBlurb: The widest language coverage here (85+), top-tier accuracy, tidy punctuation and numbers. Needs a Google account and access to the international internet.
asrProvider.geminiFileBlurb: One-shot transcription after recording. 85+ languages, custom terms supported.
asrProvider.geminiLiveBlurb: Text appears as you speak. This model does not support custom terms yet; select the entry above if you need them.
asrProvider.openrouterBlurb: One key reaches transcription models from many vendors, so switching model also switches vendor and you do not need an account with each one. Requests pass through an extra hop, making price and latency slightly higher than going direct. Its API has no hotword channel, so hotwords are not sent.
asrProvider.openaiCompatBlurb: For services not in the list above: enter the endpoint address yourself and the protocol is detected automatically. Supports self-hosted whisper.cpp, faster-whisper and FunASR, compatible services such as SiliconFlow, and Alibaba Bailian. Whether hotwords are sent depends on the detected protocol: the chat-style API sends them, the file transcription API does not.
asr.cardNameHint: Left blank, the card shows the provider name. When the same provider is configured more than once, naming each entry keeps them apart.
asr.apiUrlHint: Enter the address up to /v1; the remaining path is appended automatically. Example for a local service: http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1
asr.apiUrlOptionalHint: Left blank, the official address is used. Enter an address here when connecting through a relay or reverse proxy, up to /v1.
asr.protocolHint: OpenAI-compatible services use one of two protocols for speech. The protocol is detected automatically and remembered; select one here if the detection is incorrect.
asr.modelFreeTextHint: Enter the model name offered by this service. If you are unsure, start with the default shown in the field.

server.title: Server address
server.desc: Enter your SayIt server address. The app connects after you save.
server.help:
The default address, sayitapp.site, is a free trial server run by the author with speech recognition and AI already set up, so you can try SayIt quickly.
Running it costs money, so it isn't guaranteed to stay available.
For everyday use, run recognition locally, bring your own Doubao API key, or host the backend yourself.
server.languageNote: Affects server recognition only. Auto works for most people; choose a language if short phrases are often misdetected.

webdav.desc: Upload your settings to your own storage automatically. History and recordings are optional.
webdav.urlHint: Backups are stored in this folder, which is created if it does not exist.
webdav.jianguoyunHint: Nutstore needs an app password, generated in the desktop client under Settings → Third-party apps → Add app.
webdav.includeConfig: Settings, hotwords, text replacements, prompt presets
webdav.audioOnHint: Recordings make backups orders of magnitude larger, and every run re-uploads all of them. Free plans on services like Nutstore cap monthly upload bandwidth, which this can exhaust quickly.
webdav.keepHint: After a successful backup, the oldest copies beyond this count are deleted from the server.
webdav.restoreEmpty: No backups on the server yet.
webdav.restoreConfirmBody: {name} will overwrite this machine's configuration. Whatever the backup contains gets replaced; what it does not contain (history, if only settings were backed up) stays as it is. SayIt restarts when it finishes.
webdav.restoreDoneBody: Restarting SayIt to apply the changes…
webdav.error.urlInsecure: Plain http is not supported: WebDAV uses basic authentication, so the password would be sent in the clear. Use https instead.
webdav.error.urlScheme: The address has to start with https://.
webdav.error.unauthorized: The server rejected the account or password. Nutstore requires an app password (Account Info → Security), not your login password.
webdav.error.mkcolConflict: Could not create the folder. Create it manually in your storage, or check that its parent exists.
webdav.error.verifyMissing: The file was not on the server after uploading, so the backup did not succeed. Check whether the storage is full.
webdav.error.verifySize: The file on the server is a different size than the local one, so the backup may be incomplete. Try again.
webdav.error.emptyDownload: The download from the server was empty, so there is nothing to restore.
webdav.error.badName: That backup file name is not valid.

diagnostics.modelUnloaded: No model loaded (unloaded while idle or not used yet)
diagnostics.aiDisabledHint: AI cleanup is off, so cleanup presets and other AI-dependent features won't run. Turn it on from the top right of Home or the AI cleanup page in the sidebar.
diagnostics.faq.insertQuestion: The transcript wasn't inserted after recognition finished
diagnostics.faq.insert1: **Click the text box first** so the cursor sits inside it.
diagnostics.faq.insert2: **Don't switch windows while holding the shortcut**: the cursor must still be in the text box when you release it.
diagnostics.faq.insert3: **Nothing works anywhere**: security software is usually the cause. Add SayIt to its trusted list.
diagnostics.faq.insert4: **Games and installers fail**: they run as administrator, so run SayIt as administrator too.
diagnostics.faq.insert5: **Only one app fails**: SayIt can't recognize its text box yet. Use the copy button on the card to grab the text.
diagnostics.faq.insertFooter: Still stuck? Use "Report a problem" below and pick "Text not inserted".
